normalization_policy: normalized claim plus artifact and evidence target; no voting

findings.claim: The post-charge invalid-write recovery is contradictory and has no closed P3 entry: Section 5.2 permits POST_CHARGE_REPAIR_REQUIRED after persisted equality or strict-validation failure, while Section 9.1 assigns the same failed-validation or divergent-current condition to TRANSITION_RECOVERY_BLOCKED_DIVERGENT with DIVERGENT_CURRENT_TERMINAL_RECOVERY as its sole exit; the original intent and OPEN index entry remain unresolved, so the ordinary zero-open-intent prerequisite also prevents a separate repair intent.

locator.value: 5.2 Commit semantics step 7; 9.1 Freeze rule incomplete-intent recovery

findings.evidence_excerpt: If current ledger bytes equal neither source nor candidate, fail strict validation, or expose a partial/corrupt write, enter HUMAN-owned `TRANSITION_RECOVERY_BLOCKED_DIVERGENT`; the candidate-equality branch is inapplicable. Its sole exit is a fresh attributable HUMAN `DIVERGENT_CURRENT_TERMINAL_RECOVERY` decision
findings.impact: An implementation can select incompatible recovery edges or attempt an undeclared second write while the charge intent is still open, breaking the required lineage and risking either an untracked ledger mutation or a permanently stranded charged attempt.
findings.recommended_action: Choose one recovery state and terminal target for invalid persisted charge bytes, define the exact completion/index disposition of the original intent before any repair write, encode the repair as an explicit P3-accepted lineage edge, remove the conflicting alternative, and add source/candidate/divergent crash fixtures.

findings.claim: The charge-boundary evidence order cannot satisfy its own binding rule: the single boundary receipt is emitted before the final intent and its required administrative/index effects, but the final writer must later bind the post-append RootControlJournal current hash into that boundary aggregate while Section 5.2 forbids a replacement boundary receipt.

locator.value: 5.2 Commit semantics steps 5-6; 6.3 Bootstrap governance and accounting

findings.evidence_excerpt: Immediately before the guarded charge writer, after its own root authorization/candidate-commit and administrative authorization are appended, the coordinator re-reads the journal, recomputes exact debits/remaining ceiling and binds current root hash/sequence plus the reconciled prefix-extension proof into the boundary aggregate and `GuardedWriteReceipt`.
findings.impact: Literal validation makes every charge fail because the journal hash changed after receipt creation; relaxing equality leaves the later authorizations, intent/index effects, or accounting drift outside the claimed boundary proof and can permit charge without the complete fresh evidence set.
findings.recommended_action: Specify a non-cyclic two-stage evidence construction: freeze the exact preliminary receipt embedded in the candidate, then make a separately named final writer receipt bind all post-preliminary journal, administrative-ledger, intent, and index hashes; define which receipt authorizes charge and remove any requirement to mutate or recompute the sealed preliminary receipt.

findings.claim: The transition protocol defines recovery only when a valid intent was fully published before the OPEN append; it provides no state or authorized recovery for a partial, differing, or unreadable create-once ExecutionTransitionIntent, even though P3 scans the canonical intent root and the object cannot be overwritten.

locator.value: 9.1 Freeze rule, ordered OPEN and corruption recovery

findings.evidence_excerpt: Ordered OPEN is: (1) create-once persist and validate the intent record, then (2) version-guard append its exact OPEN entry. A crash after (1) is `INTENT_INDEX_OPEN_PENDING`
findings.impact: A crash during intent publication can leave an invalid orphan that blocks every later P3 scan, while deletion, overwrite, or omission would be undeclared; the mission can become permanently frozen or recover through an evidence-losing path.
findings.recommended_action: Add an explicit pre-charge corrupt-intent state and HUMAN-authorized, administratively accounted recovery that preserves the bad bytes, records a content-addressed tombstone or root-generation supersession, independently validates the replacement index/root view, and never charges or treats the corrupt intent as OPEN or APPLIED.
